title: Battle of the Sit River, 1238
text: February, 1238. Vladimir had fallen, and the family of the Grand Prince had burned inside its cathedral. But Yuri the Second was not in the city. Weeks earlier, he had ridden north, beyond the Volga, to raise a new army in the forests along the Sit River. Batu Khan knew he could not leave him alive. While the Mongol columns tore through Rostov, Yaroslavl and Tver, a detachment under Burundai was sent north to hunt the Grand Prince. On the fourth of March, it found him. The Persian historian Rashid al-Din recorded his fate in a single line. The emir of this province, Yurku, fled and went into the forest; he too was captured and killed. Days later, Bishop Kirill of Rostov walked the frozen battlefield, searching among the dead for his prince. He found the body, but not the head. And the next day, far to the west, Torzhok fell. The road to Novgorod lay open.
